title: Judges Chapter 5 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Judges chapter 5 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Judges Chapter 5 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Judges Chapter 5.

questions.question: Who sang on that day according to Judges 5?
questions.correctAnswer: Deborah and Barak
questions.explanation: Judges 5:1 states that Deborah and Barak the son of Abinoam sang on that day.

questions.question: Why did Deborah and Barak praise the LORD in Judges 5?
options: For the building of the temple
For the peace in the land
questions.correctAnswer: For the avenging of Israel
questions.explanation: Judges 5:2 says they praised the LORD for the avenging of Israel.

questions.question: What did Deborah say she would sing to the LORD God of Israel?
questions.correctAnswer: Praise
questions.explanation: Judges 5:3 states Deborah said, 'I will sing praise to the LORD God of Israel.'

questions.question: From where did the LORD go out causing the earth to tremble?
options: Seir and the field of Edom
questions.correctAnswer: Seir and the field of Edom
questions.explanation: Judges 5:4 mentions the LORD went out of Seir and marched from the field of Edom, causing the earth to tremble.

questions.question: Which mountains melted before the LORD according to Judges 5?
questions.correctAnswer: Sinai
questions.explanation: Judges 5:5 says the mountains melted from before the LORD, even that Sinai.

questions.question: During whose days were the highways unoccupied, and travellers walked through byways?
options: Shamgar the son of Anath and Jael
questions.correctAnswer: Shamgar the son of Anath and Jael
questions.explanation: Judges 5:6 states in the days of Shamgar the son of Anath, in the days of Jael, the highways were unoccupied.

questions.question: What ceased in Israel until Deborah arose?
questions.correctAnswer: The inhabitants of the villages
questions.explanation: Judges 5:7 tells that the inhabitants of the villages ceased in Israel until Deborah arose.

questions.question: What did the people of Israel choose that led to war in the gates?
questions.correctAnswer: New gods
questions.explanation: Judges 5:8 says they chose new gods, and then was war in the gates.

questions.question: How many shields or spears were seen among forty thousand in Israel?
questions.correctAnswer: None
questions.explanation: Judges 5:8 asks if there was a shield or spear seen among forty thousand in Israel, implying none were seen.

questions.question: To whom is the heart of Deborah inclined according to Judges 5?
questions.correctAnswer: The governors of Israel
questions.explanation: Judges 5:9 states Deborah's heart is toward the governors of Israel who offered themselves willingly.

questions.question: Who are addressed in Judges 5:10 as those who ride on white asses and sit in judgment?
questions.correctAnswer: Judges and rulers
questions.explanation: Judges 5:10 mentions those who ride on white asses, sit in judgment, and walk by the way, referring to judges and rulers.

questions.question: True or False: The earth trembled when the LORD went out of Seir and Edom.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Judges 5:4 states the earth trembled when the LORD went out of Seir and Edom.

questions.question: True or False: Deborah was called a mother in Israel after she arose.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Judges 5:7 declares Deborah arose as a mother in Israel.

questions.question: True or False: There was a shield or spear seen among forty thousand in Israel when war broke out.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Judges 5:8 says there was no shield or spear seen among forty thousand in Israel.

questions.question: True or False: The people delivered from noise of archers gathered at the places of drawing water to praise the LORD.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Judges 5:11 states they rehearsed the righteous acts of the LORD at the places of drawing water, but it does not say they gathered to praise there.

medium.title: Judges Chapter 5 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Judges Chapter 5 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Judges 5:12, what action are Deborah and Barak called to do?
options: Deborah is to awake and utter a song; Barak is to lead captivity captive
Deborah is to build an altar; Barak is to gather an army
Deborah is to write a scroll; Barak is to pray for the people
Deborah is to anoint kings; Barak is to judge Israel
questions.correctAnswer: Deborah is to awake and utter a song; Barak is to lead captivity captive
questions.explanation: Judges 5:12 commands Deborah to awake and utter a song and Barak to arise and lead captivity captive, emphasizing their roles in celebrating God's victory and leading the people.

questions.question: How does Judges 5:13 describe the dominion given by the LORD?
options: Dominion over the nobles and the mighty was given to the one who remained
Dominion was taken away from the mighty and given to the poor
Dominion was given to the kings of Canaan
Dominion was given to the priests and Levites
questions.correctAnswer: Dominion over the nobles and the mighty was given to the one who remained
questions.explanation: Judges 5:13 states that the LORD made the speaker have dominion over the mighty and those remaining have dominion over the nobles, indicating God’s empowerment of leaders to rule.

questions.question: Which tribes are mentioned in Judges 5:14 as having leaders or contributors in the battle?
questions.correctAnswer: Ephraim, Benjamin, Machir, Zebulun
questions.explanation: Judges 5:14 lists Ephraim, Benjamin, Machir, and Zebulun as tribes with roles in the battle, showing the diverse tribal participation in God's plan.

questions.question: What is described about Issachar and Barak in Judges 5:15?
options: The princes of Issachar were with Deborah, and Barak was sent on foot into the valley
Issachar refused to fight, and Barak led alone
Issachar fought from ships, and Barak delayed
Issachar and Barak stayed in the sheepfolds
questions.correctAnswer: The princes of Issachar were with Deborah, and Barak was sent on foot into the valley
questions.explanation: Judges 5:15 notes that Issachar's princes supported Deborah, and Barak was sent on foot into the valley, highlighting their active roles in the conflict.

questions.question: What does Judges 5:16 question about the tribe of Reuben?
options: Why they stay among the sheepfolds listening to flocks instead of fighting
Why they led the army into battle bravely
Why they crossed the Jordan to fight
Why they built ships to escape
questions.correctAnswer: Why they stay among the sheepfolds listening to flocks instead of fighting
questions.explanation: Judges 5:16 questions why Reuben stays among sheepfolds hearing the bleating, implying a lack of courage or involvement in battle.

questions.question: According to Judges 5:17, which tribes are mentioned as remaining inactive or distant during the battle?
questions.correctAnswer: Gilead, Dan, and Asher
questions.explanation: Judges 5:17 describes Gilead as beyond Jordan, Dan remaining in ships, and Asher staying on the seashore, indicating limited participation.

questions.question: How did Zebulun and Naphtali demonstrate their faith according to Judges 5:18?
options: They jeopardized their lives unto death in the high places of the field
They hid in the sheepfolds to avoid battle
They stayed by the seashore and did not fight
questions.correctAnswer: They jeopardized their lives unto death in the high places of the field
questions.explanation: Judges 5:18 praises Zebulun and Naphtali for risking their lives to the death at the battlefield’s high places, showing bravery and trust in God.

questions.question: What does Judges 5:19 say about the outcome of the battle at Taanach by the waters of Megiddo?
options: The kings fought but gained no money
questions.correctAnswer: The kings fought but gained no money
questions.explanation: Judges 5:19 records that the kings of Canaan fought at Taanach but took no gain of money, indicating a costly and fruitless conflict for them.

questions.question: How does Judges 5:20 describe the battle involving Sisera?
options: The stars in their courses fought against Sisera from heaven
The earth swallowed Sisera and his army
The sun stood still to aid Sisera
questions.correctAnswer: The stars in their courses fought against Sisera from heaven
questions.explanation: Judges 5:20 poetically says that the stars fought from heaven against Sisera, symbolizing divine intervention in the battle.

questions.question: According to Judges 5:21, what role did the river Kishon play in the battle?
options: It swept away the enemy forces, demonstrating God's power
It dried up and hindered Israel's advance
It was a place of refuge for Sisera
It was crossed without incident by both armies
questions.correctAnswer: It swept away the enemy forces, demonstrating God's power
questions.explanation: Judges 5:21 states the river Kishon swept away Sisera’s forces, symbolizing God’s strength in defeating the enemies.

questions.question: What happened to the horsehoofs of the enemy according to Judges 5:22?
options: They were broken by the pransings of their mighty ones
They were caught in traps set by Israel
questions.correctAnswer: They were broken by the pransings of their mighty ones
questions.explanation: Judges 5:22 says the horsehoofs were broken due to the pransings, indicating defeat and the loss of their military power.

questions.question: What does Judges 5:23 declare about the inhabitants of Meroz?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Judges 5:23 states the angel of the LORD cursed Meroz bitterly because its inhabitants did not come to help the LORD against the mighty, showing the importance of faithful support.

questions.question: Based on Judges 5:12 and 5:13, what biblical truth about leadership and victory can be applied to a believer struggling with doubt in leading others?
options: God empowers faithful leaders to have dominion and lead captives captive
Only those with noble birth can lead successfully
Leadership comes only through human strength and wisdom
Doubt should prevent believers from leading
questions.correctAnswer: God empowers faithful leaders to have dominion and lead captives captive
questions.explanation: Judges 5:12-13 shows Deborah and Barak are called to lead and given dominion by the LORD, teaching that God empowers leaders who trust Him despite challenges.

questions.question: What practical lesson about faith and action does Judges 5:18 teach through the example of Zebulun and Naphtali?
options: Faith involves risking one’s life courageously for God’s cause
Faith means avoiding danger at all costs
Faith is shown by staying distant from conflict
Faith requires only prayer, not action
questions.correctAnswer: Faith involves risking one’s life courageously for God’s cause
questions.explanation: Judges 5:18 praises Zebulun and Naphtali for jeopardizing their lives unto death, illustrating that true faith often requires courageous action.

questions.question: True or False: Judges 5:16 and 5:17 commend the tribes of Reuben, Dan, and Asher for their wholehearted participation in the battle.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Judges 5:16-17 questions why Reuben stayed among sheepfolds and why Dan remained in ships while Asher stayed on the shore, indicating a lack of full participation.

hard.title: Judges Chapter 5 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Judges Chapter 5.

questions.question: What was the reason for cursing the inhabitants of Meroz according to Judges 5?
options: They betrayed Israel to the enemy
They came not to the help of the LORD against the mighty
They refused to provide food and shelter
questions.correctAnswer: They came not to the help of the LORD against the mighty
questions.explanation: Judges 5:23 states that the angel of the LORD cursed Meroz because its inhabitants did not come to help the LORD against the mighty.

questions.question: Who is pronounced as 'blessed above women' in Judges 5?
options: Jael the wife of Heber the Kenite
The wise ladies of the city
questions.correctAnswer: Jael the wife of Heber the Kenite
questions.explanation: Judges 5:24 blesses Jael above women in the tent, recognizing her heroic act in delivering Israel.

questions.question: What did Jael give Sisera when he asked for something to drink?
questions.correctAnswer: Milk
questions.explanation: According to Judges 5:25, Jael gave Sisera milk when he asked for water, showing hospitality before her decisive act.

questions.question: How did Jael kill Sisera?
options: With a hammer and a nail
By drowning him in a river
questions.correctAnswer: With a hammer and a nail
questions.explanation: Judges 5:26 describes Jael putting her hand to the nail and striking Sisera with a hammer, piercing his temples.

questions.question: What is the literary device used in Judges 5:27 where Sisera bows and falls at Jael's feet?
questions.correctAnswer: Parallelism
questions.explanation: Judges 5:27 uses parallelism by repeating that Sisera bowed and fell at Jael's feet, emphasizing his defeat.

questions.question: What question did the mother of Sisera ask at the window?
options: Why is his chariot so long in coming?
questions.correctAnswer: Why is his chariot so long in coming?
questions.explanation: Judges 5:28 records the mother of Sisera asking why his chariot and its wheels tarry so long, showing her concern.

questions.question: What answer did the wise ladies give to Sisera's mother?
options: They have divided the prey and Sisera has received spoils
questions.correctAnswer: They have divided the prey and Sisera has received spoils
questions.explanation: Judges 5:30 shows the wise ladies answering that the spoil has been divided, suggesting a victorious outcome, which is ironic given the actual defeat.

questions.question: According to Judges 5:31, how long did the land have rest after the victory?
questions.correctAnswer: Forty years
questions.explanation: Judges 5:31 states that the land had rest for forty years following the victory described in the song.

questions.question: True or False: The phrase 'the stars in their courses fought against Sisera' in Judges 5:20 is an example of personification.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Judges 5:20 attributes active fighting to stars, a non-human entity, which is a literary device known as personification.

questions.question: True or False: Judges 5:18 praises the tribes of Zebulun and Naphtali for risking their lives in battle.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Judges 5:18 describes Zebulun and Naphtali as people who jeopardized their lives unto death in the high places of the field, showing their bravery.

questions.question: Which other Old Testament passage echoes the theme of divine intervention in battle as seen in Judges 5?
questions.correctAnswer: Exodus 14:19-20
questions.explanation: Exodus 14:19-20 describes how the angel of God and the pillar of cloud protected Israel during the Red Sea crossing, paralleling divine intervention themes in Judges 5.

questions.question: The Hebrew word translated as 'curse' in Judges 5:23 most closely means:
options: To speak evil or invoke harm
questions.correctAnswer: To speak evil or invoke harm
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'qallal' used in Judges 5:23 means to curse or bring reproach, implying invoking harm or condemnation.

questions.question: What is the significance of Jael’s actions in Judges 5:26 in the context of ancient Near Eastern warfare?
options: She defied the cultural norms by acting as a warrior
She followed the traditional role of women in battle
Her actions were typical for Kenite women
questions.correctAnswer: She defied the cultural norms by acting as a warrior
questions.explanation: Jael’s killing of Sisera with a hammer and nail was an extraordinary act of a woman taking a direct role in warfare, defying typical gender roles in the ancient Near East (Judges 5:26).

questions.question: Which New Testament passage reflects the victorious praise theme seen in Judges 5:31?
questions.correctAnswer: Romans 8:37
questions.explanation: Romans 8:37 speaks of believers being more than conquerors through Christ, echoing the victorious praise theme of Judges 5:31 where those who love God are likened to the sun in its might.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'the river of Kishon swept them away' in Judges 5:21 symbolize in the context of the battle?
options: A natural flood that hindered the enemy
The cleansing of Israel from sin
The overwhelming defeat of Sisera’s army
The crossing of the Jordan River
questions.correctAnswer: The overwhelming defeat of Sisera’s army
questions.explanation: Judges 5:21 uses the Kishon river as a symbol of God's power to sweep away Sisera’s forces, representing their decisive defeat.

theological.title: Judges Chapter 5 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Judges Chapter 5 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What divine attribute is demonstrated by the earth trembling and the heavens dropping water as the LORD went out of Seir and marched from Edom?
options: God's wrath and power over creation
questions.correctAnswer: God's wrath and power over creation
questions.explanation: Judges 5:4 describes the earth trembling and heavens dropping water when the LORD went out, showing His powerful and awe-inspiring presence as He executes judgment.

questions.question: According to Judges 5:6, what condition characterized the land during the days of Shamgar and Jael?
options: Highways were unoccupied and travellers used byways
The people worshipped only the LORD
The land was prosperous and peaceful
questions.correctAnswer: Highways were unoccupied and travellers used byways
questions.explanation: Judges 5:6 states that in the days of Shamgar and Jael, highways were unoccupied and travellers went by byways, indicating insecurity and danger in the land.

questions.question: What theological truth is taught by the phrase 'my heart is toward the governors of Israel, that offered themselves willingly among the people' in Judges 5:9?
options: The importance of willing service in leadership
The futility of human effort without God
The rejection of all earthly authority
questions.correctAnswer: The importance of willing service in leadership
questions.explanation: Judges 5:9 praises those leaders who willingly offered themselves for God's cause, teaching that willing, faithful leadership is valued by God.

questions.question: What does the command to 'Awake, awake, Deborah: awake, awake, utter a song' in Judges 5:12 signify in a redemptive-historical context?
options: A call for prophetic and victorious leadership to arise
A call to cease all warfare
A summons to mourn Israel's failures
An instruction to build a temple
questions.correctAnswer: A call for prophetic and victorious leadership to arise
questions.explanation: Judges 5:12’s call for Deborah to awake and sing, and for Barak to lead captives captive, symbolizes God raising deliverers to bring salvation, prefiguring Christ as the ultimate victorious leader.

questions.question: How do Judges 5:14-15 illustrate the doctrine of corporate responsibility among Israel's tribes during times of conflict?
options: Tribes had distinct roles and were expected to contribute to God's deliverance
Each tribe acted independently without coordination
Only one tribe was responsible for defense
The tribes rejected all forms of leadership
questions.correctAnswer: Tribes had distinct roles and were expected to contribute to God's deliverance
questions.explanation: Verses 14-15 show Ephraim, Benjamin, Machir, Zebulun, Issachar, and Reuben each playing roles in the battle, teaching that all parts of God's people have responsibility in His redemptive work.

questions.question: What attribute of God is highlighted by the stars fighting against Sisera as described in Judges 5:20?
options: God's sovereign control over cosmic powers
questions.correctAnswer: God's sovereign control over cosmic powers
questions.explanation: Judges 5:20 portrays celestial bodies fighting on God's behalf, revealing His sovereignty over all creation, including cosmic forces, to accomplish His purposes.

questions.question: Which doctrinal truth is taught by the river Kishon sweeping away Sisera's army in Judges 5:21?
options: The need for human wisdom over faith
questions.correctAnswer: God's providential judgment
questions.explanation: Judges 5:21 attributes the destruction of the enemy to the river Kishon, symbolizing how God uses natural elements providentially to enact judgment on His enemies.

questions.question: What synthesis of doctrine emerges when combining Judges 5:23's curse on Meroz with Judges 5:9's praise for willing leaders?
options: God blesses willing obedience and curses those who fail to support His cause
God is indifferent to human involvement
questions.correctAnswer: God blesses willing obedience and curses those who fail to support His cause
questions.explanation: Judges 5:9 praises willing leaders, while 5:23 curses Meroz for not helping the LORD, teaching that active obedience is rewarded and neglect is judged by God.

questions.question: How does Jael's role in Judges 5:24-27 typify Christ's victory over evil from a Christological perspective?
options: Jael's defeat of Sisera prefigures Christ's triumph over Satan
Jael's actions show human strength alone
Jael's story is unrelated to salvation history
questions.correctAnswer: Jael's defeat of Sisera prefigures Christ's triumph over Satan
questions.explanation: Jael’s killing of Sisera in Judges 5:24-27 symbolizes the decisive defeat of evil, foreshadowing Christ’s ultimate victory over Satan and sin.

questions.question: What does the imagery of Sisera's mother looking out and expecting his return in Judges 5:28-30 teach about human presumption in opposition to God's judgment?
options: Human presumption is often blind to divine defeat
Human wisdom always surpasses God's plans
questions.correctAnswer: Human presumption is often blind to divine defeat
questions.explanation: Judges 5:28-30 shows Sisera's mother expecting triumph, unaware that God's judgment has already fallen, illustrating human presumption against divine sovereignty.

questions.question: What combined theological teaching do Judges 5:2 and Judges 5:31 convey about God's deliverance and blessing upon His people?
options: God avenges Israel and blesses those who love Him with peace
God is neutral in Israel's conflicts
God punishes Israel for their sins without relief
God's blessing is unrelated to faithfulness
questions.correctAnswer: God avenges Israel and blesses those who love Him with peace
questions.explanation: Verse 2 praises the LORD for avenging Israel, and verse 31 blesses those who love Him, showing God's justice coupled with peace for the faithful.

questions.question: What does Judges 5:8 teach about Israel's spiritual condition before Deborah arose, in relation to idolatry and warfare?
options: Israel had turned to new gods leading to internal conflict and military weakness
Israel was united under one god
Israel rejected all forms of war
questions.correctAnswer: Israel had turned to new gods leading to internal conflict and military weakness
questions.explanation: Judges 5:8 states Israel chose new gods, leading to war and absence of weapons among 40,000 men, indicating spiritual apostasy causing societal breakdown.

questions.question: What doctrinal insight about God's justice and human responsibility can be derived from the curse upon Meroz in Judges 5:23?
options: God holds those accountable who neglect to aid His cause against evil
God does not involve Himself in human affairs
God blesses those who remain neutral
God is indifferent to human actions
questions.correctAnswer: God holds those accountable who neglect to aid His cause against evil
questions.explanation: Judges 5:23 curses Meroz for not helping the LORD, teaching that God demands active participation in opposing evil and holds people accountable for omission.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that the victory over Sisera was merely a natural military success. What does Judges 5:19-22 actually teach about the nature of this victory?
options: The victory was divinely orchestrated, involving heavenly forces and natural elements
The victory was only due to human tactics
The battle was insignificant and unremarkable
questions.correctAnswer: The victory was divinely orchestrated, involving heavenly forces and natural elements
questions.explanation: Verses 19-22 depict kings fighting, stars fighting from heaven, and the river Kishon sweeping away enemies, teaching God's active intervention in the victory.

questions.question: How does Judges 5:10-11 emphasize God's righteousness and faithfulness in the context of Israel's deliverance?
options: God's righteous acts are to be recounted where the people are delivered from danger
God only works through human strength
God's acts are hidden and mysterious
questions.correctAnswer: God's righteous acts are to be recounted where the people are delivered from danger
questions.explanation: Verses 10-11 speak of those who escaped archers recounting the LORD's righteous acts, emphasizing God's justice and faithfulness in salvation.
